newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-NATAL KEEP SOUTH AFRICA IN SUPER 12 HUNT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NATAL KEEP SOUTH AFRICA IN SUPER 12 HUNT.

text.p: South Africa's Natal scraped a draw on Sunday to join an Australasian trio in the Super 12 championship semifinals.
The 27-27 stalemate with Northern Transvaal ensured Natal line up with Auckland, Wellington and Australian Capital Territory in the last four.
Their three points from the match -- two for the draw and one for their tally of four tries - was enough to put them out of reach of Northerns and Gauteng Lions in the table.
Auckland guaranteed themselves a home semifinal and maintained a nine-point lead in the standings by beating Wellington Hurricanes 45-42 on Saturday.
The Blues had to contain a furious onslaught by the Hurricanes in the final quarter but outscored their visitors by six tries to five.
Auckland remained unbeaten in the tournament with nine wins and a 40-40 draw with Northern Transvaal.
Wellington must now fbeat second-placed ACT in Wellington on May 18 to move above them r them and land the other home tie.
ACT beat Waikato 48-34 in Canberra on Friday to move into second place with their seventh victory.
Gauteng Lions conclude their campaign against Natal at Ellis Park next weekend, no doubt glad to be back on home soil after a disastrous run of four defeats in New Zealand and Australia.
Against Queensland in Brisbane Ray Mordt's men managed four tries, to earn the only point of their Australasian trip, but lost 40-27.
In Dunedin, New South Wales carried too much fire-power for Otago and won 27-16 to move eighth. Canterbury improved to sixth with a 16-11 win over Free State in Bloemfontein.
